correctness.rationale: Every real parameter and all leaf counts covered: an orthogonal neutral dark-space decomposition reduces the matrix to a 4x4 polynomial whose squared-energy roots have negative product when W and gamma are positive. Distinct roots prove both the nonreal pair and diagonalizability, while a direct trimer nilpotency/rank argument establishes its third-order exceptional point. Exact expansions and strict imaginary-growth monotonicity follow from the same quadratic. Independent symbolic/finite numerical checks passed, but finite numerical checks are only supplementary.

originality.rationale: The closed quartic, all-weighted-star zero threshold, absence of exceptional points for all nonzero passive coupling, and singular passive-spoke unfolding are not stated or implied by the directly inspected path, metric-star, or coupled-chain/plaquette sources. value.rationale: The minimal passive-leaf modification of the familiar gain/loss trimer changes a genuine PT real-spectrum interval into a thresholdless broken phase with no exceptional point, for all degree and all nonzero real neutral couplings. The theorem isolates a topology-driven singular physical stability mechanism, gives explicit growth rates, and distinguishes a quarter-power law in squared neutral hopping at the old third-order exceptional point from ordinary square-root branches away from it. This structural exact graph-family result is not an arbitrary isolated parameter computation.
